issues.legal_issue: A declaratory suit is not time-barred merely because an adverse revenue entry or an earlier compromise existed for many years when the asserted right was first clearly threatened by a later refusal and the suit was filed within three years of that threat.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed ownership and joint possession of land, including a share obtained under a written compromise that had been presented to and acted upon by the High Court.
The revenue records showed the defendants as owners of a share that the plaintiffs claimed should belong to them.
The plaintiffs pleaded that they first learned of the incorrect entries about a week before filing suit and that the defendants then refused to admit their claim or join in correcting the entries.
The suit was filed about eighteen years after the compromise, and the courts below treated the compromise date as the date the right to sue accrued.

The Supreme Court held that the suit could not be treated as time-barred on the pleaded facts; whether the compromise had been acted upon and whether possession had been delivered remained matters for determination on remand.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the suit was barred by limitation was set aside. On the pleaded facts, the right to sue accrued when the defendants refused to admit the plaintiffs’ claim, about a week before suit was filed, so the suit could not be held time-barred merely because it followed the compromise after many years. The matter was remitted for decision on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 58 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the three-year period for a declaratory suit begins when the right to sue first accrues. A right to sue accrues when the asserted right is infringed or there is a clear and unequivocal threat to infringe it; the mere existence of an adverse revenue entry does not itself create a cause of action. The Court relied on Mt. Bolo v. Mt. Koklan (AIR 1930 PC 270) and C. Mohammad Yunus v. Syed Unnissa (AIR 1961 SC 808), which state this accrual principle.

rule.if: declaratory_suit and asserted_right_exists and (right_infringed or clear_unequivocal_threat) and suit_filed_within_three_years_of_trigger

predicates.declaratory_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking a declaration of a claimed right.
predicates.asserted_right_exists: The claimant asserted a right that could be infringed or threatened by the opposing party.
predicates.right_infringed: The opposing party acted in a way that infringed the claimant’s asserted right.
predicates.clear_unequivocal_threat: The opposing party clearly and unequivocally threatened to infringe the claimant’s asserted right.
predicates.suit_filed_within_three_years_of_trigger: The claimant filed suit within three years after the infringement or clear threat occurred.

issues.definition: When a claimant brings a declaratory suit asserting a right, that right is infringed or clearly threatened, and suit is filed within three years of that trigger, the suit is not barred by limitation.
